items.title: Specified regulated generalized entropy
items.physical_scope: A model definition on one fixed smooth classical Lorentzian background and one specified compact spacelike section of a smooth null hypersurface. It assigns finite generalized-entropy sums to named finite tensor factorizations and assigns a renormalized value only when that exact sequence converges finitely in its declared scheme. It does not assert that the factors approximate a continuum field algebra, that a different regulator or counterterm choice gives the same value, that matter changes the background geometry, or that the quantity is monotone along a physical process.
items.statement:
Fix a smooth, oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, its metric-selected connection, and one smooth embedded null hypersurface $\mathcal H\subset M$. Use the null-hypersurface convention in the mathematical definition of the smooth null screen family. Supply a smooth, nonzero, future null generator field $k$ tangent to $\mathcal H$ with $\nabla_k k=0$. Choose a nonempty compact smooth embedded spacelike two-surface $\Sigma\subset\mathcal H$ transverse to $k$, meaning $T_p\Sigma\oplus\mathbb Rk_p=T_p\mathcal H$ at every $p\in\Sigma$. If $i:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M$ is inclusion, the induced metric $h=i^*g|_{T\Sigma}$ is positive definite. In any local surface chart $(y^1,y^2)$, define its area density by $\mu_h=\sqrt{\det(h_{AB})}\,|dy^1dy^2|$ and set $A_\Sigma=\int_\Sigma\mu_h$. Admissible model data require $0<A_\Sigma<\infty$.

A named finite-regulator sequence consists of labels $(\Lambda_n)_{n\ge1}$, nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_{\mathrm{in},n}$ and $H_{\mathrm{out},n}$, and a density operator $\rho_n$ on the ordered tensor product $H_{\mathrm{in},n}\otimes H_{\mathrm{out},n}$ for each $n$. The physical Boltzmann constant $k_B>0$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, while $c>0$ and $\hbar>0$ have units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and $\mathrm{J\,s}$, respectively. Define

$$S_{\mathrm{out},n}:=S_{\mathrm{out}}(\rho_n;H_{\mathrm{in},n},H_{\mathrm{out},n}),\qquad S_{\mathrm{gen},n}[\Sigma]:=S_{\mathrm{grav},n}[\Sigma]+S_{\mathrm{out},n}.$$

Here $S_{\mathrm{out},n}$ is the finite spectral entropy of the partial-trace state specified by the finite-regulator outside-entropy definition, using natural logarithms and $0\log 0:=0$. The assigned geometric value $S_{\mathrm{grav},n}[\Sigma]$ is finite and has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$; its terms, including every chosen local counterterm and finite normalization condition, are fixed as part of the declared scheme. Any dimensional regulator label has its units recorded with that scheme.

On the optional area-term branch, one allowed summand of $S_{\mathrm{grav},n}[\Sigma]$ is

$$\frac{k_Bc^3A_\Sigma}{4G_{\Lambda_n}\hbar},$$

where each $G_{\Lambda_n}>0$ is specified model data with the units of Newton's constant, $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$. The relation of $G_{\Lambda_n}$ to the reference $G_N$ is also declared model data. The renormalized generalized entropy $S_{\mathrm{gen}}^{\mathrm{ren}}[\Sigma]$ is defined exactly when the sequence $(S_{\mathrm{gen},n}[\Sigma])_{n\ge1}$ converges to a finite real value in the declared scheme; its value is that limit. If the sequence has no finite limit, this definition assigns no renormalized value. The limit belongs only to the named sequence and scheme.

With the physical $k_B$, both terms in each sum have units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, and $A_\Sigma$ is in $\mathrm{m^2}$.

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III Black Holes, University of Cambridge lecture notes (2024)
references.locator: Complete 149-page PDF; §§10.8–10.9, printed pp. 146–147, equations (10.110)–(10.113) and the backreaction qualification: the stationary area coefficient, the generalized-entropy sum, and the limits of the summary.

references.title: Aron C. Wall, A proof of the generalized second law for rapidly changing fields and arbitrary horizon slices, Physical Review D 85, 104049 (2012), arXiv:1105.3445v6
references.locator: Complete article; §1, equations (1)–(3), and §2.1–2.8, especially §§2.5–2.8: outside-entropy divergence, specified renormalization, and the distinct hypotheses of the conditional GSL proof.

items.title: Generalized entropy requires a separate physical inequality
items.physical_scope: A conditional finite-data comparison for the regulated generalized-entropy definition at one fixed section and in one declared scheme, with a common finite geometric contribution, one-dimensional input factor, and two constant finite-regulator state sequences. It shows only that the additive definition and geometric area information do not impose monotonicity on the outside entropy. The sequence labels do not denote physical time, and the item asserts no empirical result or violation of a physical generalized second law.
items.statement: The calculation compares two independent sequences of model data at one fixed section. A monotonicity claim for a specified family of cuts would require an ordered parameter set $J\subseteq\mathbb R$, a section $\Sigma_s$ and a regulator/state/geometric sequence at each $s\in J$, finite convergence at each $s$ if renormalized values are used, and a proof that $S_{\mathrm{gen}}^{\mathrm{ren}}[\Sigma_{s_2}]\ge S_{\mathrm{gen}}^{\mathrm{ren}}[\Sigma_{s_1}]$ whenever $s_1\le s_2$ in $J$. None of this comparison data or inequality is part of the fixed-section definition or supplied by the finite example.

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III Black Holes, University of Cambridge lecture notes (2024)
references.locator: Complete 149-page PDF; §§10.8–10.9, printed pp. 146–147, equations (10.110)–(10.113); the concise GSL summary is contextual, not the basis of this item's conditional claim.

references.title: Aron C. Wall, A proof of the generalized second law for rapidly changing fields and arbitrary horizon slices, Physical Review D 85, 104049 (2012), arXiv:1105.3445v6
references.locator: Complete article; §§2.1–2.8, especially §2.8: the GSL argument is conditional on semiclassical, horizon-algebra, and renormalization assumptions; the finite data comparison here is not such a physical evolution.
